thread:
Alex T.: heads-up — running into a gap with alert weighting when we backfill historical incidents for new operators. routing ends up over-notifying a single oncall.
Maria G.: can you paste an example? is this when operator backfill sets weight=1 by default?
Alex T.: yeah, we backfilled last 90d, everything got 'operator=primary' and weight wasn't set. so the notify fanout treats them as high priority -> duplicate pages.
Dylan: oof. we've seen similar with tenant backfills. short-term we can dedupe by fingerprint and short TTL, but that hides the underlying routing logic mismatch.
Riya: what's the desired behaviour? prefer spread across fallback tiers or reduce weight on backfilled ops?
Alex T.: prefer: backfill records should default weight=0.3 and route through soft-fanout (no immediate page) unless the signal repeats in <10m. that keeps historical noise out.
Sam: sounds reasonable. Need to confirm no downstream systems assume weight=1 when absent.
Maria G.: +1 on redacting backfill as non-urgent by default. also we should add a small boolean flag to mark 'historical_import' so console shows it.
Dylan: API change: add optional header X-Import-Stamp or body field import_type=historical with default weight fallback. simple shim in notify router.
Alex T.: quick config snippet I tested:

```
# example notify policy fallback
match: {source: operator, import_type: historical}
actions:
  - set_weight: 0.3
  - route: soft-fanout
  - dedupe_ttl: 600
```

Sam: can we express that as a per-route rule in console UI? Product wants editable presets for import/backfill handling.
Riya: UX note — console should show a small pill "imported" and in the alert timeline show original sample time vs import time, so SREs can triage.
Maria G.: telemetry question — if we lower weight, does our alert burn metric still count towards tenant error budgets? we need separate tracking.
Dylan: yes, currently burn metrics are computed before notify weighting. we'd either filter those or emit a separate metric group import.burn.* — easier: emit import=false for normal burn, import=true for backfills, then rollups ignore import=true by default.
Alex T.: agree. also add an opt-in to include import.burn in monthly exports for audits.
Sam: implementation plan: (1) API field + header (Dylan), (2) notify-router shim to apply weight/policies (Alex/Sam), (3) metrics tagging and count change (Dylan), (4) console indicator + preset (Maria/Riya). estimate: 2 sprint work.
Riya: UI mock: show inline toggle in routing rule: [Treat historical imports as low urgency] with info tooltip.
Maria G.: policy question: will there be exceptions where backfilled incidents must page? e.g., legal/sev for payment regressions.
Alex T.: yes — policy can include allowlist: if tag:pay-regression OR severity>=P1 then ignore import flag. we'll include that in router match.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled for notify-router shims at 2025-03-12T03:00Z (canary -> prod), runbook: #eng-oncall
Dylan: I'll open a small RFC outlining signal naming, metric tags, and sample queries. link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/imported-alerts
Sam: can we add a test in the chaos-sim harness to ensure we don't reduce paging coverage for real-time alerts? want to avoid false negatives.
Alex T.: yes, add a smoke test that flips import flag and asserts paging suppressed for single-occurrence alerts but not for repeated ones.
Maria G.: OK let's sync tomorrow 10am PT to walk the RFC and UX mock. thanks all :party_parrot:
